units.title: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation

questions.stem: Equal positive charges of $2.0\,\mu\text{C}$ are placed at three corners of a square of side $0.30\,\text{m}$, the fourth corner being vacant. What is the electric field at the centre of the square?

options.label: A
options.text: $4.0\times10^{5}\,\text{N C}^{-1}$, directed towards the vacant corner

options.label: B
options.text: $4.0\times10^{5}\,\text{N C}^{-1}$, directed away from the vacant corner

options.label: C
options.text: $2.0\times10^{5}\,\text{N C}^{-1}$, directed towards the vacant corner

options.label: D
options.text: Zero, because the three remaining charges are placed symmetrically about the centre

questions.stem: What is the electric potential at a point on the equatorial line of an electric dipole of moment p, at distance r from its centre?

A thin ring of radius 4 cm carries a charge of 1 μC spread uniformly. A point charge of 1 μC is placed on the axis of the ring 3 cm from its centre. What is the magnitude of the force on the point charge?
Using the graph of the potential energy of a dipole in a uniform field shown in the figure, how much work must be done to turn the dipole slowly from θ = 60° to θ = 180°?
A slab of dielectric constant 3 is placed perpendicular to a uniform electric field of 6 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. What is the electric field inside the slab?
Two point charges of +2 μC each are 40 cm apart. How much work must an external agent do to bring them slowly to 20 cm apart?

Consider the following statements about electric charge.
A. The total charge of an isolated system remains constant in every process.
B. A body that becomes negatively charged gains a tiny amount of mass.
C. Quantisation of charge means that charge can only be a positive whole-number multiple of e.
D. A body carrying +5 μC and −2 μC has a net charge of +3 μC.
Choose the correct option.
How many electrons must be added to a neutral body to give it a charge of −1 μC?
Which of the following best describes the emf of a cell?

options.label: A
options.text: The force with which the cell pushes electrons round the circuit

options.label: B
options.text: The terminal potential difference when the cell supplies its maximum current

options.label: C
options.text: The total chemical energy stored in the cell

options.label: D
options.text: The work done by the cell per unit charge in taking charge from its negative to its positive terminal, equal to its terminal voltage on open circuit

questions.stem: Points a and b are joined by three branches. Branch 1 has a 12 V cell in series with $2.0\,\Omega$, branch 2 has a $4.0\,\Omega$ resistor, and branch 3 has a 6.0 V cell in series with $3.0\,\Omega$. The positive terminals of both cells are towards a and the cells have negligible internal resistance. What is the current in the $4.0\,\Omega$ resistor, from a to b?

A current of 1.5 A flows from point A to point B along a branch containing, in order from A, a $3.0\,\Omega$ resistor and then a cell of emf 8.0 V and internal resistance $1.0\,\Omega$. The current enters the cell at its negative terminal and leaves at its positive terminal. What is $V_A - V_B$?

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements:
A. Magnetisation is the net magnetic moment per unit volume of a material.
B. Magnetic susceptibility has no unit.
C. Magnetic intensity H and magnetisation M have the same SI unit.
D. For vacuum the magnetic susceptibility is 1.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem: An electron with speed $3.0\times10^{6}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ enters a uniform magnetic field of $2.0\times10^{-3}\,\text{T}$ with its velocity at $30^{\circ}$ to the field. What is the pitch of its helical path? ($m_e = 9.1\times10^{-31}\,\text{kg}$, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$)

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements:
A. Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops.
B. The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
C. Magnetic field lines start from north poles and end on south poles inside the magnet.
D. Inside a bar magnet the field lines run from the south pole to the north pole.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem: A long solenoid carrying a steady current is suspended so that it can turn freely in a horizontal plane. What does it do?

options.label: B
options.text: It comes to rest along the north–south direction, like a bar magnet

options.label: C
options.text: It comes to rest along the east–west direction

options.label: D
options.text: It stays in whatever direction it was left

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem: A charged particle moves through a region containing only a uniform magnetic field. What is the work done on it by the magnetic force?

options.label: A
options.text: Positive if the particle is positively charged

options.label: B
options.text: Equal to qvB multiplied by the distance moved

options.label: C
options.text: Negative if the particle moves against the field

questions.stem: The figure shows the field $dB$ at point P on the axis of a circular loop due to the element $dl$ at the top of the loop. Which expression gives the component of $dB$ along the axis?

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem: Two long wires pass through a closed loop: one carries 5 A upward and the other 3 A downward. A third wire carrying 4 A upward lies outside the loop. The loop is traversed so that upward current counts as positive. What is the value of the line integral of B around the loop? (Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{T m A}^{-1}$.)

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A charged particle projected into a uniform magnetic field always moves in a circle.
Reason (R): The magnetic force on a moving charge is always perpendicular to its velocity.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem: Two coils have a mutual inductance of 1.5 H. If the current in the primary coil rises steadily from 0 to 20 A in 0.5 s, the magnitude of the emf induced in the secondary coil is

A 100-turn coil of area $100\,\text{cm}^2$ and resistance $5\,\Omega$ lies with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T. It is pulled completely out of the field in 0.2 s, and a charge $q_1$ flows through it. In a repeat of the experiment it is pulled out in 2 s, and a charge $q_2$ flows. Which of the following is correct?

A metal rod of length 0.6 m rotates with an angular speed of $50\,\text{rad s}^{-1}$ about an axis through one of its ends, in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T. The emf induced between the ends of the rod is
The coil of a simple AC generator rotates at $1500$ revolutions per minute. What is the frequency of the emf it produces?

Assertion (A): The heating effect of an alternating current is described by its rms value rather than by its average value.
Reason (R): The average of a sinusoidal current over a complete cycle is zero, whereas the heat produced in a resistor depends on the square of the current.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem: A $100\,\text{W}$ point source radiates all its power uniformly as electromagnetic waves. What is the amplitude of the electric field at a distance of $2.0\,\text{m}$? ($c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\,\text{C}^{2}\,\text{N}^{-1}\,\text{m}^{-2}$)

In the figure, loop C surrounds the wire leading to the left plate of a capacitor that is being charged. S1 is the flat disc bounded by C; S2 is a pot-shaped surface with the same rim whose bottom lies between the plates. Which description of what crosses each surface is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: S1: displacement current only; S2: conduction current only

options.label: B
options.text: S1 and S2: conduction current only, so the magnetic field on C is the same

options.label: C
options.text: S1: conduction current; S2: nothing at all, so the magnetic field on C must be zero

options.label: D
options.text: S1: conduction current only; S2: displacement current only, and the two are equal

Taking $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\,\text{C}^2\,\text{N}^{-1}\,\text{m}^{-2}$, the displacement current is about

A plane electromagnetic wave of intensity $600\,\text{W m}^{-2}$ is fully absorbed by a surface of area $0.20\,\text{m}^{2}$ over $5.0$ minutes. What momentum is delivered to the surface? ($c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$)
At a certain instant, the conduction current in the wire charging a parallel-plate capacitor is 3 mA. What is the displacement current between the plates at that instant?

options.label: B
options.text: zero, because no charge crosses the gap

options.label: C
options.text: less than 3 mA, because the gap opposes the current

options.label: D

In a double slit experiment the fringe width is 2.0 mm. The distance of the fifth dark fringe from the central bright fringe is

A plane wavefront in air enters glass (n = √3) with its rays at 60° to the normal. In the Huygens construction, the ratio CE/AB of the width of the refracted wavefront to that of the incident wavefront is

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about light passing from air into glass.
A. Its frequency does not change.
B. Its wavelength becomes smaller.
C. Its speed becomes smaller.
D. Its wavelength becomes larger.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

Which of the following are advantages of a reflecting telescope over a refracting telescope of the same aperture?
A. Its objective produces no chromatic aberration.
B. A paraboloidal mirror objective is free from spherical aberration.
C. The mirror can be supported over its entire back surface, so very large apertures are practical.
D. It always gives an erect final image.

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem: The work function of a metal is 2.48 eV. What is its threshold wavelength? (Take hc = 1240 eV nm.)

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem: De Broglie explained Bohr's quantisation rule by requiring a whole number of wavelengths to fit around the orbit, $2\pi r = n\lambda$. The radius of the n-th Bohr orbit of hydrogen is $r_n = n^2 a_0$ with $a_0 = 0.529\times10^{-10}\,\text{m}$. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron in the n = 3 orbit?

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The graphs of stopping potential against frequency for two different metals are parallel straight lines.
Reason (R): For light of a given frequency above threshold, the photoelectric current is directly proportional to the intensity of the light.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem: What is the minimum energy that must be given to a hydrogen atom in its ground state to raise it to its second excited state?
In the figure, the electron of a hydrogen atom jumps from the n = 3 orbit to the n = 2 orbit. Which statement about this jump is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: A photon of 12.09 eV is absorbed by the atom

options.label: B
options.text: A photon of 1.89 eV is emitted; it is the Hα line of the Balmer series

options.label: C
options.text: A photon of 1.89 eV is emitted; it belongs to the Lyman series

options.label: D
options.text: No photon is involved because both orbits are stationary states

questions.stem: According to de Broglie's explanation of Bohr's quantisation condition, how many complete de Broglie wavelengths of the electron fit around the circumference of the third Bohr orbit of hydrogen?
Which property of the nuclear force explains why it has practically no effect between nucleons that are more than a few femtometres apart?

options.label: B
options.text: It is repulsive at very small separations

options.label: C
options.text: It is much stronger than gravity

questions.stem: A p-n junction diode is said to be forward biased when it is connected with:

options.label: A
options.text: its p-side to the positive terminal and its n-side to the negative terminal of the battery

options.label: B
options.text: its p-side to the negative terminal and its n-side to the positive terminal of the battery

options.label: C
options.text: both its sides to the positive terminal of the battery

options.label: D
options.text: its p-side to the battery and its n-side left unconnected

questions.stem: A semiconductor has a forbidden gap of 1.8 eV. What is the longest wavelength of light that can create electron-hole pairs in it? (Take $h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\,\text{J s}$, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.)

A rectifier is fed with a sinusoidal input of frequency $f$ and peak voltage $V_m$ (ideal diodes; for the centre-tap circuit, $V_m$ is the peak voltage of each half of the secondary). Match each quantity in List-I with its value in List-II.

left: A. Ripple frequency of a half-wave rectifier
B. Ripple frequency of a full-wave rectifier
C. Peak inverse voltage across each diode of a centre-tap full-wave rectifier
D. Average output voltage of a half-wave rectifier

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The reverse saturation current of a junction diode increases when its temperature rises.
Reason (R): The depletion region of a junction diode widens when the reverse bias voltage is increased.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
